agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `regsafe()` function in the BPF verifier incorrectly treats special negative range values representing `BEYOND_PKT_END` as standard integers during comparison, failing to distinguish them from normal pointer ranges.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds a guard clause `if (rold->range < 0 || rcur->range < 0)` to enforce exact equality for negative range values, correcting the logic where `rold->reg->range == BEYOND_PKT_END && rcur->reg->range == N` previously allowed `regsafe()` to return true due to flawed numeric ordering.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes BPF verifier safety check to correctly handle special packet-end sentinel values during register state range comparison
intent_record.what: Modified the range comparison logic in regsafe() to add a special case check for negative range values before comparing rold->range > rcur->range
intent_record.how: Prevents incorrect comparison of special sentinel values (negative ranges representing BEYOND/AT_PKT_END) by requiring exact equality when either range is negative, while preserving the original greater-than comparison only for non-negative ranges

grouping_result.intent: Fixes BPF verifier safety check to correctly handle special packet-end sentinel values during register state range comparison

vuln_statements.stmt_text: return memcmp(rold, rcur, offsetof(struct bpf_reg_state, var_off)) == 0 &&
vuln_statements.explanation: This memcmp comparison checks register state equality up to the var_off field offset. A vulnerability here could allow the BPF verifier to incorrectly accept unsafe state transitions by not properly validating all critical register fields (particularly var_off), potentially enabling out-of-bounds packet memory accesses through flawed range validation logic.

The range_within() check validates whether packet pointer ranges remain safe across program transformations. Combined with the memcmp above, any flaw in this range validation could permit unsafe state transitions that bypass proper bounds checking for BPF packet data access.
